title: RLM: Recursive Language Models for Large Codebases - Shashi, Superagentic AI

primary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk introduces RLM as a general agent architecture pattern emphasizing recursive delegation via llm_query and a REPL-based harness for programmable context management. RLM is demonstrated on codebase tasks typical of coding assistants, RLM Code is a developer tool, and the pattern is described as generally applicable. The talk introduces a research pattern from an MIT paper and demonstrates a reference implementation with a live demo. Requires prior understanding of coding agent harnesses, context management, and recursive delegation. Conference-style talk with live CLI and TUI demonstration on a real repository. All evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript.

summary:
The talk addresses a fundamental problem: coding agents perform well on small repositories but degrade as context grows in large monorepos. Existing approaches include grep-based search, semantic search, context compression, and memory solutions, but each has limitations. The speaker introduces Recursive Language Models (RLM), a pattern from an MIT paper, whose core thesis is to externalize context management into a programmable execution environment. Rather than loading everything into the model's context window, the repository is treated as structured data that the model can operate on. The model writes code in a REPL to inspect, slice, and compute relevant chunks, producing bounded observations fed into the main context. When more information is needed, the model recursively delegates focused sub-questions via llm_query to another language model environment, and the loop continues until a final synthesized result is returned.

The speaker uses an analogy of a lead engineer assigned to a new large codebase: rather than reading line by line, the engineer makes notes, writes scripts to search, and asks specialists when stuck. The recursion mirrors this specialist consultation. Codebases are chosen as the demonstration scenario because they are structured data with directories, tests, imports, dependencies, and configs—not just text.

RLM Code, an independent open-source reference implementation by Superagentic AI, demonstrates the pattern. It uses RLM concepts as-is—recursive calls and REPL execution—while adding flexibility for local or cloud models and any observability framework. The speaker notes that official RLM implementations exist (RLM, RLM minimal, and DSPy-based by Omar), but emphasizes RLM is a pattern implementable in various ways. The live demo uses Gemini with a Docker sandbox, showing the full loop: REPL code generation, evidence building, llm_query calls, and final answer. Trajectories are captured in JSONL format for import into any observability platform. The terminal UI harness shows recursion depth, token usage, rewards, and event timelines.

Real-world use cases include root cause analysis, repository onboarding, and unfamiliar codebase exploration. The speaker observes that proprietary managed agent frameworks are reportedly using RLM concepts: the Codex harness writes Python code in a REPL to curate context (described as one form of RLM), Gemini managed agents use RLM concepts, and dynamic multi-agent workflows where one agent spawns sub-agents in separate sandboxes derive from RLM ideas. Anthropic's cloud code engineers have reportedly acknowledged on X that they use RLM concepts. The talk concludes by encouraging adoption of RLM concepts on large-context repositories and inviting audience questions.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
